idiom_name: Immer produce() for runtime sharing + readonly/Readonly<T>/as const for compile-time immutability
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds the compile-time half of the pattern to the JavaScript runtime: readonly properties, Readonly<T>, ReadonlyArray<T>/as const and the Readonly<T> that Object.freeze is typed to return make 'nobody writes through this handle' checkable, turning an accidental in-place update into a type error instead of a silent aliasing bug. The runtime sharing comes from the same library realization as JavaScript - Immer's produce() copies only the changed path and freezes the result - while structuredClone is typed as a deep copy for values that must not be shared at all. Classic refcounted copy-on-write is not available; the type layer plus structural sharing is what replaces it.
pitfalls: readonly is compile-time only and vanishes at runtime: a cast to a mutable type or a plain-JS consumer can still write through it, so pair it with Object.freeze at trust boundaries.
Readonly<T> is shallow - nested objects stay mutable unless a deep readonly type is used - and as const is not deep immutability either.
Immer's draft is mutable by contract, so typing the recipe parameter as readonly forces casts and defeats the library.
Spreading a readonly array into a new one copies the array (cheap) but shares the elements, which must then be treated as immutable.
